title: Full Stack Development Readiness
description: Test your end-to-end knowledge spanning UI state, server endpoints, CORS, database integration, and deployment.

questions.question: What is the purpose of CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) headers?
options: To allow or restrict resources requested on a web page from another domain outside the origin
To speed up database indexing on the server
To compress static asset bundles before transmission
To automatically authenticate users using browser biometric credentials
questions.explanation: CORS is an HTTP-header based mechanism that allows a server to indicate any origins other than its own from which a browser should permit loading resources.

questions.question: Where is the safest place to store sensitive session tokens (like JWT) in a modern web application to prevent XSS theft?
options: In `localStorage`
In `sessionStorage`
In an `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, and `SameSite` cookie
In a global JavaScript variable window.__TOKEN
questions.explanation: HttpOnly cookies cannot be accessed by client-side JavaScript, preventing malicious XSS scripts from reading and exfiltrating the token.

questions.question: In Next.js or fullstack React frameworks, what is the primary difference between Server Components and Client Components?
options: Server Components render strictly on the server and send zero JavaScript to the client bundle
Client Components cannot make fetch requests
Server Components cannot access environment variables
Client Components run directly inside the Node.js runtime on the server
questions.explanation: React Server Components (RSC) execute exclusively on the server, allowing direct database access while keeping client bundle sizes lightweight.

questions.question: What is 'Optimistic UI' updating in frontend-backend integration?
options: Updating the client UI immediately assuming the server request will succeed, rolling back if it fails
Waiting for all background API jobs to finish before showing any UI
Automatically retrying failed HTTP requests indefinitely
Minifying HTML files to reduce loading times
questions.explanation: Optimistic UI provides instant visual feedback to users by updating UI state before the server response returns, reverting on error.

questions.question: Which HTTP header is sent by browsers during a CORS preflight request?
options: OPTIONS
HEAD
TRACE
CONNECT
questions.explanation: Browsers automatically send an HTTP OPTIONS request to the server to check if the cross-origin request is allowed before sending the actual request.

questions.question: When designing a relational database for a blog with Users and Posts (1 User has many Posts), where does the foreign key belong?
options: In the `posts` table referencing `users(id)`
In the `users` table referencing `posts(id)`
In a separate many-to-many junction table
In neither table; relational databases do not use foreign keys
questions.explanation: In a one-to-many relationship, the 'many' side (posts) holds the foreign key `user_id` pointing to the 'one' side (users).

questions.question: What is the key advantage of using GraphQL over traditional REST endpoints?
options: Clients can request precisely the fields they need, preventing over-fetching and under-fetching
GraphQL automatically writes database SQL queries without a backend
GraphQL replaces the need for server-side validation
GraphQL eliminates the need for database indexes
questions.explanation: GraphQL enables client-specified queries to retrieve exact data requirements in a single round-trip, avoiding redundant payload overhead.

questions.question: What is the primary role of a reverse proxy like Nginx in a production full stack deployment?
options: Terminating SSL/TLS, load balancing traffic, and serving static files efficiently
Executing frontend React component code
Managing relational database transaction isolation levels
Compiling TypeScript code into JavaScript on the fly
questions.explanation: Nginx sits in front of backend application servers to handle SSL termination, load balance incoming web traffic, and rapidly serve static assets.

questions.question: What is database connection pooling and why is it crucial for fullstack backends?
options: Reusing a set of pre-established database connections to avoid the high latency of opening a new TCP handshake on every request
Backing up database tables to multiple cloud storage buckets
Clustering multiple database servers into a single shard
Compressing JSON payloads before sending to the client
questions.explanation: Establishing TCP and SSL connections to a database is expensive; connection pools maintain active connections ready for immediate reuse.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a Webhook?
options: A server-to-server HTTP POST push notification triggered by an event in a third-party service (e.g., Stripe payment)
A browser extension that intercepts user clicks
A CSS hook that styles React components dynamically
A Git command used to resolve merge conflicts
questions.explanation: Webhooks are user-defined HTTP callbacks that enable platforms (like Stripe, GitHub) to notify your server immediately when an event occurs.
